repair.term: The Repair Table: Balancing a Dish
repair.definition: The diagnostic chart taped inside every seasoned cook's skull — symptom, then levers, in order of gentleness. TOO FLAT: salt first; if salted, acid; if bright, umami (the three-axis check). TOO SALTY: dilute (unsalted liquid, more base), bulk (starch, cream), or counter (acid and a touch of sugar bend perception; the potato myth mostly dilutes). TOO SOUR: fat and sweetness buffer; baking soda neutralizes chemically (pinches only — it eats brightness); time mellows. TOO SWEET: acid cuts, salt reframes, bitterness opposes (coffee, cocoa, char), heat distracts. TOO BITTER: salt suppresses, sweet buffers, fat rounds, acid brightens past it. TOO SPICY: dairy and fat dissolve capsaicin, sugar soothes, acid refocuses, starch dilutes — and volume of bland base is the honest fix. TOO RICH: acid, always acid — then something crunchy-fresh. MUDDY/OVER-DEEP: brightness at the top — fresh herb, zest, raw allium; the layers entry's finishing register, applied as medicine. The meta-rule: adjust in small moves, taste after EACH, and fix the loudest fault first — most 'complicated' problems are one lever pulled twice.

protocol.definition: The palate is a muscle with a vocabulary problem — you cannot improve what you cannot name. THE TRAINING PROTOCOL: taste ANALYTICALLY (before swallowing, ask the five-taste checklist, then aroma families, then texture and temperature, then finish — thirty seconds of attention beats thirty mindless meals), taste COMPARATIVELY (two olive oils side by side teach more than twenty alone; the wine wing's method generalized to vinegars, salts, chocolates, soy sauces), taste SINGLE INGREDIENTS at their extremes (a caper, a raw cranberry, straight fish sauce — calibrate the instruments), and RETASTE your own dishes at every stage and at table temperature. THE VOCABULARY LADDER: start with the axes (salty/sweet/sour/bitter/umami + rich/bright/hot), add the registers from this atlas (nutty, floral, briny, funky, smoky, resinous, green), then borrow wine's structure words (attack, body, finish, length). Write tasting notes — writing forces naming, naming builds memory. The professional endpoint: the chef who can say 'it needs mid-palate umami and a brighter finish' instead of 'something's off' fixes dishes in one move instead of five — and trains a whole kitchen to taste in the same language. The palate you build is the only knife that never dulls.

metaRule: Adjust in small moves and taste after each one. Fix the loudest fault first — most complicated problems are one lever pulled twice.

faults.label: Flat
faults.symptom: The flavours are all present and none of them arrives. Tastes like a photograph of the dish.

levers.note: Always first. Most flat dishes are unsalted dishes.
If it is already salted, this is the next lever — not more salt.
If it is salted and bright and still flat. The three-axis check ends here.

faults.label: Salty
faults.symptom: It reaches for the water glass before the second bite.

levers.note: Unsalted liquid, or more of the base.
Starch or cream — volume the salt has to spread through.
Acid and a touch of sugar bend the perception. The potato trick mostly just dilutes.

faults.label: Sour
faults.symptom: The acid arrives before anything else and stays after everything else has gone.

levers.note: Buffers rather than removes.
The other buffer. Below the threshold of tasting sweet.
Neutralises chemically. Pinches only — it eats brightness along with the fault.
Mellows on its own, if you have any.

faults.label: Sweet
faults.symptom: Cloying by the third mouthful, and nothing cuts through it.

levers.note: Cuts.
Reframes — the same sugar reads as seasoning rather than dessert.
Opposes it directly. Coffee, cocoa, char.
Distracts from it.

faults.label: Bitter
faults.symptom: A hard edge at the back of the palate that stays after swallowing.

levers.note: Suppresses bitterness outright. Real chemistry, not folklore.
Buffers.
Rounds it off.
Brightens past it rather than removing it.

faults.label: Spicy
faults.symptom: The heat has stopped being a flavour and become the only one.

levers.note: Dissolves capsaicin. This is the one that physically removes heat.
Soothes.
Refocuses the palate elsewhere.
Dilutes.
The honest fix, and usually the only one that works at service.

faults.label: Rich
faults.symptom: Delicious for two bites and fatiguing by the sixth.

levers.note: Always acid. There is no second answer to this one.
After the acid, not instead of it.

faults.label: Muddy
faults.symptom: Deep, brown, and indistinct — every layer present and none of them legible.

levers.note: Fresh herb, zest, raw allium. The finishing register, applied as medicine.
